summary: Multipath KV-cache divergence causes intermittent pinned-session split and oscillating fallback routing
description: Issue summary: During a staged canary rollout of gptx-13b-rev1 for NimbusHealth, a subset of tenant sessions were intermittently routed to a fallback model. Investigation shows the root symptom is a divergence between KV prefix caches on different multipath routes, causing session pin decisions to disagree and the routing layer to oscillate between pinned and fallback variants. Customers reported mixed outputs and increased latency for a small cohort.
impact: Approximately 3% of the customer's traffic in us-east experienced mixed-model responses and elevated tail latency (p95 increased from 180ms to ~750ms) over a 45-minute window. No data loss. Customer-facing quality regressions for affected sessions; higher error rate observed in orchestration logs (HTTP 502/504) around the same timestamps.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a canary rollout for gptx-13b-rev1 with multipath prewarm enabled and cohort sampling at 2%.
2) Send a consistent stream session for a tenant with session affinity pinned to the canary cohort.
3) Observe the edge-proxy logs for parallel prewarm probes; watch KV cache keys on two different routing paths (edge A vs edge B) diverge in TTL/state.
4) When one path returns a stale/missing prefix entry while the other has a prewarmed prefix, orchestrator's pin-consensus logic can fail and route to fallback variant intermittently.
5) Reproduce by toggling a simulated prewarm delay on one path (see test harness in PR 4591).
logs: Attached excerpts: edge-proxy logs show alternating route decisions for session token=eyJ... between route-72 and route-88 at 2026-03-12T14:03:21Z; serving-runtime shows KV cache miss for prefix 'tenant/nh-42/session/abc' on route-88 while route-72 reports cache hit; orchestrator emitted 'pin-consensus-mismatch' traces and returned fallback policy 0x3 at the same time. Relevant trace IDs: trace-7a9f2c, trace-7a9f2d. Full logs uploaded to s3://redwood-support/SUP-704555/log-bundle.tar.gz

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: multipath prewarm optimization causes non-deterministic ordering of KV writes and TTL updates across parallel edge paths. Orchestrator expects eventual KV consistency within pin-grace window; when divergence exceeds grace window pin consensus fails and fallback routing is selected. Additional contributing factor: health-probe-induced eviction on one path produced a cache miss while other path retained warmed state. Reproduced with local harness by introducing 150-400ms write delay on one prewarm worker. Correlation with edge-proxy version v2.18 where multipath batching behavior changed.
comments: 2026-03-12 14:15 - Support (Aisha): Notified NimbusHealth and requested traffic sample and session tokens. Asked customer to reduce canary percentage while we investigate.
2026-03-12 14:40 - SRE (Diego): Reproduced in staging with simulated prewarm delay. Confirmed mismatch in KV TTL writes between parallel paths. Creating INT ticket to track orchestration fix.
2026-03-12 15:06 - Support (Aisha): Applied mitigation for NimbusHealth (disabled multipath prewarm for their cohort). Customer reports reduction in mixed-model responses within 3 minutes.
2026-03-13 09:22 - Eng (Priya Rao): Patch in runtime to add a short pin-consensus barrier and align prefix TTL writes. PR 4591 opened for review and backport to 2.18-hotfix branch.
2026-03-13 12:04 - Customer (NimbusHealth - Ops): Confirming improved behavior after mitigation. Asked for timeline for permanent fix and whether dedicated clusters require config change.
resolution: Mitigation: disabled multipath prewarm for affected cohort and forced single-path routing for NimbusHealth while fix is staged. Permanent fix: engineering implemented pin-consensus barrier and TTL-alignment in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4591; this prevents consensus mismatches during prewarm writes and handles transient probe-evictions gracefully. Hotfix deployed to edge-proxy v2.18.1 in us-east and rolled to affected dedicated clusters. Observed fallback rate returned to baseline within 8 minutes of deployment.
follow_up:
1) Backport hotfix to previous maintenance branches and schedule rollout to eu-west where multipath is enabled.
2) Add an automated runbook check to detect KV TTL divergence across edge paths and create an alerting rule.
3) Update canary configuration docs to recommend single-path prewarm for cohorts with strict pinning requirements.
4) INT-2107 tracks adding a consensus health-check during orchestrator snapshot commit.
next_steps: Runnightly canary with multipath prewarm disabled by default until backport is in all regions
